note: Six post-inverted-span-fix runs of mbenchmark.py over the 3-case multi-file corpus (model claude-opus-4-8, cap 5, plateau 2), 2026-06-13. Recorded to characterize run-to-run variance: a single live run is one stochastic sample, not the result. These six rows are hand-recorded from the printed mbenchmark.py output, not auto-emitted; only the most recent run is independently corroborable from the gitignored on-disk maggregate.json, and the other five rows are not regenerable from a retained artifact. Retaining per-run snapshots or a fixed seed is a v3.1 item.
stable_findings: Every run improved all 3 cases over baseline; baseline never returned; zero regressions.
Generation 1 alone removes roughly 79 to 104 percent of the original-to-floor span on every case, every run.

Every returned best lands at or below the reference floor (flagged suspiciously-simple or fragmentation-smell) in 17 of 18 case-runs; the one exception, task_scheduler run 1, returned a best at 98.2 percent of the original-to-floor span (about 1.8 percent above the floor).
unstable_findings: One-shot versus needs-generation-2-or-more flips run to run; only 1 of 6 runs had all 3 cases one-shot.
feedback_gain_pp ranges from 0 to about 24 percentage points for the same case across runs, dominated by where stochastic generation 1 landed.
